memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "Abraham lived a hundred and seventy-five years. Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man and full of years; and he was gathered to his people" - Gen 25:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham's long journey comes to a close. He dies "at a good old age... full of years." What a beautiful way to describe a life — not merely long in days, but full. Abraham had walked with God through failures and faith, through waiting and promises, and he ends satisfied.

The phrase "gathered to his people" is the Bible's gentle way of saying that death was not the end for him. Abraham was going to join those who had gone before — a quiet hint that he was held by God even in death. Long before the resurrection was fully revealed, God was the God of Abraham, "not the God of the dead but of the living" (Matt 22:32).

Abraham did not receive everything God promised in his lifetime; he died still trusting, looking ahead to a city whose builder is God (Heb 11:10, 13). His faith reached beyond the grave.

A "full" life is not measured by wealth, comfort, or years alone, but by a life lived in faith with God. However many days we are given, we can aim to be "full of years" — full of God's presence, full of trust, full of purpose. And for those who belong to Christ, the best is always still ahead.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What would make your life "full" in God's eyes, not just long?
Are you trusting God even for promises you may not see fulfilled in your lifetime?
How does the hope beyond death change the way you live today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to live a full life of faith in You, whatever my number of days. Thank You that in Christ, death is not the end but a gathering into Your presence. Amen.
